title: Element algebraic over a subfield
statement: Let $E/F$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], with structure homomorphism $F\to E$. An element $\alpha\in E$ is *algebraic over $F$* if it is a root of some nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $F$: there is $P\in F[t]$, $P\neq0$, with $P(\alpha)=0$ in $E$ (the coefficients mapped to $E$ by $F\to E$). The extension is *algebraic* if every element of $E$ is algebraic over $F$. In particular, a field $\Omega$ of characteristic $0$ is an extension of $\mathbf Q$ through the unique ring homomorphism $\mathbf Q\to\Omega$ (onto its prime subfield), and '$z\in\Omega$ is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$' is meant for this extension.
